question:
Simplify:

sqrt3(sqrt12 - sqrt27)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simplify the terms inside the bracket first by factoring out perfect squares.

√12 = 2√3 and √27 = 3√3

Given expression: √3 × (2√3 − 3√3)

⇒ √3 × (−√3) = −3

**∴ The correct answer is -3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: √3(√12 − √27)

**Calculations:**

We can solve this by distributing √3 to each term inside the bracket.

⇒ √3 × √12 − √3 × √27

Using the root property √a × √b = √(a × b):

⇒ √(3 × 12) − √(3 × 27)

⇒ √36 − √81

Since 36 and 81 are perfect squares:

⇒ 6 − 9

⇒ −3

**∴ The correct answer is -3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Surds (Roots)

Multiplication of surds follows the rule: √a × √b = √(ab).

Simplification of Surds

To simplify a square root, factor the number into its prime factors and pull out pairs of identical factors as a single number outside the root. Example: √(x²y) = x√y.

BODMAS Rule

Always solve Brackets first, then Orders (powers/roots), followed by Division/Multiplication, and finally Addition/Subtraction.
